name: Sunniva Okoro-Brandt
description: Considered the architect of what critics call 'neural realism,' Sunniva Okoro-Brandt spent two decades directing licensed neural-feed dramas that prioritized authentic emotional texture over narrative spectacle, insisting on using non-actor subjects alongside trained talent and minimal neural enhancement in post-production. Her trilogy on grief and displacement — completed in 2201 — is studied in every licensed film program in Meridian 88. She now works as a consultant for Vantablack's prestige division while quietly funding independent projects under a pseudonym.
cultural_impact: Neural realism — her aesthetic philosophy — became the dominant language of prestige neural-feed production, even as she moved further from the mainstream she created.
story_hooks: Okoro-Brandt's pseudonymous project turns out to be a documentary on Vantablack's neural-lock contract practices — using subjects she met through her legitimate consulting work.
A player is approached to courier funding from Okoro-Brandt to an underground director, not knowing what they're carrying or who it's from.
A young director claims Okoro-Brandt stole the core concept of their underground project for a licensed production — and wants proof before they go public.
